ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the lower part of the figure there is a horizontal table or board surface, marked with conductor coil a; coil a is drawn as a horizontally placed closed circular ring; directly above circular ring a there is a vertically placed solenoid, marked as b, and the axes of the two coincide. On the right side of the solenoid is connected a circuit; in the figure a power supply symbol and a vertical sliding rheostat can be seen, and the slider is marked as P. Reasoning: According to the circuit shown in the figure, when slider P slides downward, the resistance connected into the circuit by the sliding rheostat becomes smaller, so the current in solenoid b increases. The increase of the solenoid current makes the magnetic flux passing through the lower closed circular ring a increase. According to Lenz's law, the induced current generated in coil a must hinder this increase in magnetic flux, so coil a and solenoid b behave as mutually repelling each other. Since solenoid b is above a and fixed, the direction of the magnetic force on coil a is downward. The pressure of coil a on the table is equal to its weight plus the effect of the downward magnetic force, so the pressure FN increases.
